newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Bolger says stronger economy means stronger NZ dlr.
newsitem.headline: Bolger says stronger economy means stronger NZ dlr.

text.p: Prime Minister Jim Bolger, commenting on exporter concern about the rising New Zealand dollar, said on Wednesday a steady appreciation of the currency would occur as the economy strengthened.

Bolger said in a radio interview that the New Zealand dollar was not strong in historical terms. "I think the real concern of exporters I have spoken to is not the strength per se but the speed at which it increased over the last six to 10 months and I can understand that. It appreciated very rapidly. But a steady appreciation of the New Zealand currency will occur as the New Zealand economy strengthens," he said.
He said the exchange rate cut both ways because it lowered the cost of goods in New Zealand as well as affecting exports.

"When I came into parliament in the mid seventies the New Zealand dollar was worth almost twice what it is worth today against the U.S. dollar. You could get $1.20 in the United States for a New Zealand dollar...and we get 69 cents or 70 cents today."
Asked how he saw an export economy surviving another world downturn, Bolger said if there was another world downturn "my guess is that we would do much much better (than in past recessions)".

"The protections we had, the subsidies we had,...didn't help us in the last world downturn. We lost thousands of jobs. We were not able to continue with the commercial life of New Zealand as before and we lost all those jobs.
"We have much greater strength...and wider diversity of product in the economy.
"I believe it would survive a world downturn much better."
He said removing subsidies and tariffs created a "win-win" effect because poorer families could buy better quality products. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473 4746
